penetration_assumption: NOT a penetration model — there is no new-line demand to model, so a penetration number would be invented. The figure is an observed-run-rate recovery: 68 packaged-food SKUs (excluding the noodle family) each sold in >=3 distinct months of the 12-month window, are currently at zero on-hand, and have been out >=21 days. Their realised net sales were Rs 1,34,271 (VERIFIED). Annualising each SKU's own active-month run rate over 12 months gives Rs 3,64,788, i.e. Rs 2,30,517 of theoretical headroom at a VERIFIED 16.9% blended margin = Rs 39,072 gross profit (VERIFIED query). I then apply a judgement discount of ~35% for within-brand substitution — a buyer denied Dabur Honey 650g takes the Dabur Honey 250g that is in stock — giving ESTIMATED Rs ~1.5 L revenue / Rs ~25,000 gross profit. The 35% discount is my judgement, not measured; that is the softest part of this number and the reason the rupee figure is weaker than the verdict. The noodle family is excluded entirely (7 SKUs, Rs 96,123 headroom, Rs 10,639 GP) because it is fully substitutable on-shelf: Maggi Atta 72.5g was out for 182 days while the category still GREW 28% YoY and Maggi 48g Masala sold 34,045 units. Counting it would be double-counting sales ARY already made.
probe_evidence: Every one of the 53 researched lines is LISTED at ARY. The coverage diff reported 0 missing and 53 covered, but its evidence is unusable in BOTH directions — 30 of 53 lines are "broad" matches on words like 'rice', 'tomato', 'chilli', 'masala', 'atta', 'apple', 'plus', and its "specific" matches include Honey matched on 'zandu' (Zandu Balm) and Peanut butter matched on 'protein'. Four line pairs share identical SKU/sales figures (106 SKUs/Rs 14.2L on 'rice' appears on 4 different lines), so I rebuilt the probe from scratch. My own first universe repeated the trap: 'hakka' matched Raja SHAKKAR and group 128 Frozen held paneer — Rs 5.5 L of contamination I removed. TWO CANDIDATE GAPS DIED ON PROBE: (1) RTE retort veg curries — the diff matched 'rajma' to raw rajma BEANS in Pulses, but `ary assort probe "paneer butter" "dal makhani" retort` found MTR Paneer Butter Masala 300g (06V1), MTR Palak Paneer 300g (0C5T), MTR Mutter Paneer 300g (0C9Y), MTR Shahi Paneer (00CT), MTR Dal Makhni 300g (0C9X), MTR Chana Masala 300g (00CO) all LISTED and ACTIVE in sub-group 'Ready To Cook'. The purchase ledger shows why they are dead: ~60 units bought ONCE on 2024-03-15, all-time sales Rs 6,650, last sale 2024-10-20, never reordered. Tried and abandoned, not missing. (2) RTE rice meals/khichdi — MTR Veg Pulao 250g (Rs 1,170 all-time), Daawat Biryani Kit and Daawat Cuppa Schezwan Rice both 6 units in 2023. Everything else probes as present AND selling: Korean ramen (the research's "best margin in this lane") = Geki 3 flavours Rs 36,120 + Nissin Rs 8,520; Knorr cup-a-soup Rs 61,479; Nutella Rs 67,720; Dabur/Jivo honey Rs 79,265; Kissan mixed-fruit jam Rs 54,713; peanut butter Rs 23,531; Lizzat/Sunil papad Rs 40,749; ketchup 8g sachets 27,875 units; full Veeba mayo range; and even the research's "line nobody else sells" Himachali lingdi pickle (Minchy's Lungru Pickle 500g). Direct SQL absence test over 33 terms returns ZERO SKUs for only: barbecue sauce, hummus, pesto, couscous, khakhra, thepla, marmalade — every one a line the demand research itself flags as slow/dead-stock risk. VERIFIED CATEGORY STATE (live window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31, feed live to 2026-08-30): 948 SKUs listed, 946 active, 350 sold, Rs 20,31,847 net of GST (Rs 21.48 L gross, returns Rs 5,041), 596 active SKUs sold NOTHING, 407 never sold ever, 339 never purchased ever, only 178 hold stock today, and 202 of the 350 that DO sell (57.7%) are at zero on-hand. Shop-wide control: 51.8% — so this is a shop-wide condition, only slightly worse here; the top-200 sellers are only 27.5% out, so the collapse is in the tail. Category is GROWING 28.1% YoY (Rs 16.76 L to Rs 21.48 L gross) with monthly selling-SKU count up from 84-118 to 110-156. MARGIN, derived from the live purchase ledger not a blanket rate: Rs 19,45,834 net sales vs Rs 16,93,339 COGS at weighted-average PurchaseDetail cost across 310 SKUs = 12.98% VERIFIED. Two tax traps had to be fixed to get there — PurchaseDetail.ItemValue is tax-EXCLUSIVE (IncludeInRate=false) while SaleDetail.FinalSaleAmount is tax-INCLUSIVE (a naive comparison reads 17.66%), and SaleDetail.TaxAmount is the TOTAL GST of which TaxAmount1/TaxAmount2 are the CGST/SGST halves, so summing all three deducts tax twice (reads 7.72%). Correct net is TaxableValue1.
kill_reason: There is no assortment gap in packaged food, and adding SKUs here would destroy value. Three independent proofs. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING: all 53 researched lines are listed; the only terms returning zero SKUs are barbecue sauce, hummus, pesto, couscous, khakhra, thepla and marmalade — long-tail items the research itself calls dead-stock risk. (2) THE MISSING THINGS WERE TRIED AND DIED: the RTE retort line I initially flagged as a genuine gap is fully listed (MTR 300g pouches, 6 SKUs), bought once in March 2024, sold Rs 6,650 all-time, never reordered. Recommending it would be exactly the "add a SKU already listed but never stocked" error. (3) THE STRUCTURAL REASON — and this is the finding that should change the buying plan: ARY's prepared-food counters sell Rs 54,21,642 net from 46 SKUs, 2.7x the entire 350-SKU packaged-food category's Rs 20.3 L. Chinese Items alone (cooked noodles, momos) does Rs 24.4 L; Steam Momos (Rs 4.27 L gross) outsells the whole ketchup+sauce+mayo+jam+pickle+papad shelf combined. On a closed campus with mess food plus a hot counter, a Rs 80-100 hot plate beats a Rs 120 ambient retort pouch every time — which is precisely why the MTR pouches died in 2024 and why 63% of this category's active SKUs sold nothing in 12 months. The category is not starved; it is growing 28% YoY on Rs 10 impulse SKUs (Maggi 48g, ketchup sachets, Knorr Rs 10 soup) and its own bestsellers ARE in stock. The residual money is availability in the tail, and it is small: Rs ~1.5 L revenue / Rs ~25,000 gross profit against a Rs 7.67 Cr business — 0.2% of turnover. Against the research fleet's implied ambition this is a null result, and it is the correct one.

blockers: MARGIN IS HALF WHAT THE RESEARCH ASSUMED. VERIFIED 12.98% from the purchase ledger against demand-research bands of 10-35%. The specific claims do not survive: Korean ramen, called 'the best margin in this whole lane' at 20-35%, actually returns 10.1-14.6% at ARY (Geki 80g). Branded MRP-locked lines run 11-14% (Maggi 11.7%, Nutella 13.3%, Kissan jam 11.0%). Only unbranded/local earns real money — Raja Nutri 28.8%, Foodcoast ketchup sachet 21.7%, Savour Macroni 20.9%, Sunil Papad, Jadugar Poha 19.1%. Any growth plan for this category should be a LOCAL-SOURCING plan, not a brand-listing plan.

CANTEEN CANNIBALISATION IS THE STRUCTURAL CEILING. Rs 54.2 L from 46 prepared-food SKUs vs Rs 20.3 L from 350 packaged SKUs (both VERIFIED, net of GST, same window). Ambient meal solutions cannot win against a hot counter on a closed campus. This is not a merchandising problem to be fixed; it is the correct equilibrium, and it is why the retort line died.

BELOW-COST PRICING MUST BE FIXED BEFORE ANY RESTOCK. 9 SKUs sell below cost. Rajdhani Daliya 1 Kg alone is -Rs 7,576/yr and is simultaneously the biggest out-of-stock line in the category — the single most tempting 'availability win' in the data is a loss-maker. Reorder without repricing and the availability fix reduces gross profit.

CATALOGUE BLOAT IS THE REAL OPERATING COST. 596 of 946 active SKUs sold nothing; 407 never sold ever; 339 were never purchased. The dormant set is mostly the same product re-keyed at each new pack size or spelling (Dabur Honey 12 listings, Kissan Jam 12, Dr.Oetker peanut butter 340g x3 dormant while 400g sells). Every one has to be priced, counted and shelved at stock-take. Delisting is worth more operator time here than any buying decision.

REORDER DISCIPLINE, NOT SUPPLIER REACH, IS THE CONSTRAINT. Every SKU on the restock list has a supplier already invoicing ARY within the last 12 months, so 40 km of Rajgarh hill road is not the blocker. Items sit out 88-295 days with no reorder while the same vendor delivers other lines — Kissan Tomato Sauce sold in 10 of 12 months and is still out 88 days. There is no reorder-point discipline below the top ~200 SKUs (27.5% out) versus the tail (57.7% out).

DATA CAVEATS ON THIS ANALYSIS. (a) Stock.Quantity is summed across all 12 warehouses; a SKU stocked at Ary Warehouse but absent from Ary Pos reads as in-stock here, so the 57.7% out-of-stock figure is if anything conservative for the shop floor. (b) SaleHeader has no cancel flag; returns were checked separately and are immaterial at Rs 5,041. (c) The Rs 1.5 L / Rs 25,000 recovery carries a 35% substitution discount that is my judgement, not a measurement — the verdict is high-confidence, the rupee figure is medium. (d) I could not test whether stockouts push spend off-campus rather than to a neighbouring SKU; that needs a counter conversation, not a query.
